clue.text: Honour among thieves

blocks.note: surface reading: the proverbial code of loyalty that criminals keep with one another
setter's reading: in card games a court card is an honour, and this one is the nursery-rhyme character who stole some tarts

explanation.surface: The old saying that even criminals keep faith with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge and whist the top cards are called honours; the Jack of Hearts, in the nursery rhyme, stole the Queen's tarts, so he is a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A playing-card honour that is also a famous rhyme thief, so it is literally an honour belonging to thieves.

clue.text: Baggy clothes for New Yorkers

blocks.note: first meaning: loose breeches gathered at the knee
second meaning: a nickname for New Yorkers, from the Dutch settlers of old New Amsterdam

explanation.surface: Loose garments worn by people from New York.
explanation.definitionFit: The garment word doubles as the old nickname for descendants of Dutch settlers in Manhattan, popularised by Washington Irving.

clue.text: It may be liquid donkey consumed audibly

indicators.note: audibly tells us to go by how the words are spoken, not by their spelling

blocks.note: a donkey is an ass, and consumed is ate, said in the British way as 'et'

explanation.surface: A cryptic picture of a donkey slurping something wet.
explanation.walkthrough: Many British speakers pronounce 'ate' as 'et', which makes ASS ATE sound like ASSET.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid asset is property easily turned into cash, so an asset is something that may be described as liquid.

clue.text: Level passed — just

blocks.note: level means flat or equal
passed something over to someone

explanation.surface: Something went by on the level, and only just.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'barely' but is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fair and impartial treats both sides alike, which is the sense of the adjective just.

clue.text: Acquires understanding in depth

blocks.note: first meaning: works something out, gets to the bottom of it
second meaning: units of six feet used for measuring water depth

explanation.surface: Someone comes to grasp a subject thoroughly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In depth' reads as 'thoroughly', but it is a measurement: depth given in fathoms.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means works out or comprehends, and the plural noun is the nautical unit by which sea depth is reckoned.

clue.text: Important chap accepting a payment in advance

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a man's name, the one punned on in the title of Wilde's comedy about importance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A self-important man takes a deposit up front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Important' points to Oscar Wilde's comedy The Importance of Being Earnest, whose title puns on the name Ernest.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest money is a deposit paid beforehand as a pledge that a bargain will be completed.

clue.text: Flower-girl stood up in the window

blocks.note: first meaning: the garden bloom
second meaning: got to one's feet
also a girl's name
and the round stained-glass window of a cathedral

explanation.surface: A girl selling flowers got up and stood at the window.
explanation.walkthrough: Four meanings in one: the bloom, the girl's name, the past tense of rise, and the circular church window.
explanation.definitionFit: The bloom is a garden favourite, and the past tense of rise means got to one's feet.

clue.text: Enormous hit mother's idol appears in likewise

indicators.note: appears in says one thing shows up inside another

blocks.note: so means likewise, as in 'so do I'
ma is mother, plus the 's
an idol is a hero

explanation.surface: A huge hit record features a mother's favourite star.
explanation.definitionFit: Smasheroo is slang for an outstanding success, the same as a smash hit.

clue.text: Unable to catch kid identified to police?

blocks.note: a young goat, which butts, so humorously a butter
to finger someone is to inform on them to the police

explanation.surface: A child was named to the police and could not get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but it is the young goat, an animal that butts; 'butter' is read as one who butts.
explanation.definitionFit: A butter-fingered person is clumsy and keeps dropping things, especially a fielder dropping catches.

clue.text: Policeman restricts parking within popular zone

indicators.note: restricts means hems in, so one item is held inside the other

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
a sector is a zone or area
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A police officer controls parking in a busy area of town.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is a rank of police officer above sergeant in British forces.

clue.text: Chaos as fun characters go dancing

indicators.note: letters that go dancing move about and end up in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Mayhem as cheerful types head off for a night out dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Snafu is military slang for a situation in total disorder or confusion.

clue.text: Top man on board to make picture of boat

blocks.note: the king is the top piece on a chessboard, K in chess notation
to etch is to make a picture by engraving

explanation.surface: The captain sketches a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top man on board' suggests a ship's captain, but the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel, so it is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Means of cooking duck and some venison

indicators.note: some means only part, so the word is cut short and its tail dropped

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like the letter O
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: A recipe calling for duck and a bit of deer meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is a cricket score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven is a heated enclosed appliance in which food is baked or roasted.

clue.text: Crack marksman

blocks.note: first meaning: an attempt, as in have a crack at
second meaning: someone who shoots

explanation.surface: An expert sharpshooter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' reads as an adjective meaning expert, but it is the noun for a try.
explanation.definitionFit: A try at something is a go or attempt, and a person who fires a gun skilfully is called a good one.

clue.text: Airway's security flap as one pilot gets clobbered

indicators.note: something clobbered is battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A security flap on an airline as a pilot gets beaten up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airway' suggests an airline, but it is the windpipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The epiglottis is the cartilage flap that closes over the windpipe during swallowing to keep food out.

clue.text: Seamen giving assessments of the Channel

blocks.note: first meaning: ordinary sailors in the navy, as opposed to officers
second meaning: audience figures measuring a TV channel's popularity

explanation.surface: Sailors reporting on conditions in the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Channel' suggests the English Channel, but it is a television channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval sailors below officer rank are called ratings, and viewing figures for broadcasts go by the same word.

clue.text: Convert trams for rerouting around north

indicators.note: rerouting sends the trams along a new path, so their letters change order
around says one piece is wrapped about another

blocks.note: the letters of these two words
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Trams are diverted around the northern part of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is part of the fodder, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To transform something is to change it completely into another form, the same as converting it.

clue.text: One who gradually gets to the point as bringer of light?

definitions.text: One who gradually gets to the point

blocks.clueFragment: One who gradually gets to the point
blocks.note: first meaning: someone or something that narrows steadily to a point
second meaning: someone carrying a slender candle in a procession

explanation.surface: A slow-talking person likened to someone carrying a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets to the point' suggests coming to the main issue at last, but it means growing narrower.
explanation.definitionFit: A taper is a thin candle, so one who bears it brings light, and to taper is to narrow toward an end.

clue.text: Stone-throwers in the animal kingdom

blocks.note: first meaning: ancient siege catapults that hurled rocks
second meaning: wild asses of Asia

explanation.surface: Creatures in nature that hurl stones.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman catapult was named after the wild ass because of its violent kick.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an Asian wild ass and a Roman siege engine for hurling rocks.

clue.text: Let it be! Issue is something for the head to take on

definitions.text: something for the head to take on

blocks.note: stet is the proofreader's instruction meaning let it stand
issue means offspring, and a son is one

explanation.surface: A boss is told to leave a problem be and to take it on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take on' sounds like tackling a task, but here it means putting on.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is a broad-brimmed cowboy hat, which a person puts on the head.

clue.text: Rising, perhaps, to embrace old gentlemen

perhaps signals that the letters may be arranged otherwise

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The plural is Italian: signori, the form of address for gentlemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Signori is the Italian plural of signor, the title used for men, equivalent to gentlemen or sirs.

clue.text: Deliver a television without charge

blocks.note: a television set
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: An offer to bring a TV round at no cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliver' suggests bringing goods, but it means rescue or release.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone from danger or captivity is to release or liberate them.

clue.text: Such a small confection requires light touch

blocks.note: first meaning: a small sweet or meringue bearing this name
second meaning: a gentle brush of the lips

explanation.surface: A dainty cake needs a delicate hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sugary sweet such as a chocolate drop is called this, and the word also means a gentle touch of the lips.

clue.text: Points way to building by Wren?

definitions.note: the question mark flags the bird, not the architect

blocks.note: two compass points, north and east
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Directions to one of Christopher Wren's churches.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral; here the wren is the little bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bird such as a wren constructs a home of twigs and moss in which to lay eggs.

clue.text: Outstanding triumph encompassed by own goal initially

a triumph is a win
opening letter of this word

clue.text: Account of players embracing opponents
